claims: A stallion is an uncastrated adult male horse.
Stallions possess a crestier neck due to testosterone.
Stallions have higher testosterone levels compared to geldings or mares.
Testosterone makes stallions more fiery or aggressive.
In the wild, stallions are protective of their mares and territory.
The primary role of stallions is breeding.
Stallions require registration in a studbook to be considered an approved sire.
A gelding is a castrated male horse.
A colt is a young uncastrated male horse usually under 3-4 years.
